## What is R Markdown?

R Markdown is a way to combine plain text, R code, and math in one file. When you knit it, R runs the code and turns the file into an HTML report.

The code and explanation stay together, so the analysis can be rerun and the results updated from the same document.

## A quick math example

Inline math looks like this: $\alpha + \beta = \gamma$.

A displayed equation looks like this:

$$
\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i
$$

## Explore the data

```{r}
data(mtcars)
head(mtcars)
summary(mtcars$mpg)
```

## Weight and MPG

```{r}
plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg,
     main = "Weight vs MPG",
     xlab = "Weight",
     ylab = "MPG")
```
